step1_analysis.description: A differential amplifier stage with active loads, likely part of a limiting amplifier chain used to convert bursty input signals to CML levels in a 1.25-Gb/s GPON receiver.

paper_reference.title: A 1.25-Gb/s Burst-Mode Receiver for GPON Applications

voltage_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the amplifier stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm * Rout, typically 10-20 dB per stage for limiting amplifiers.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard differential pair with active load in 130nm CMOS.
Required to support the 1.25 Gb/s data rate without excessive intersymbol interference.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the stage.

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly given for this single stage

sky130_expected.reasoning: A typical high-speed limiting amplifier stage draws a few mA from a 1.8V supply.

settling_time.description: Time required for the output to settle during a burst.

sky130_expected.calculation: Simulated transient response to a step input.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Comparable to the reported burst-mode settling time in the paper.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure AC gain, bandwidth, transient swing, and DC power consumption. Note: VSS is set to 1.8V to properly bias the PMOS sources, and resistors are added to fix floating nodes caused by extraction errors.
